source_text:
Ἀντιοχεῦσι καὶ πάσῃ τῇ οἰκουμένῃ. ἀπρεπὲς οὖν ταύτα διδάσκειν ἑτέρους, ὧν τῆς
ἐπιμελείας ἀπέστης καὶ ἰδίῳ κατέλυσας δόγματι. Gal 2,19– Ὁ νόμος τῶν σωματικῶν
ἔχει τὴν ἐργασίαν καὶ τὴν ἀπόλαυσιν, τόδε φάγε καὶ τόδε μὴ φάγῃς, σάββατον
τήρησον, περιτομήν. ἡ χάρις οὐ βούλεταί σε διὰ τούτων εὐδοκιμεῖν. ἐνεκρώθην οὖν,
φησί, τούτοις. τί χρείαν ἔχω νόμου; Ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός. ὃ ἐγὼ
ἔζων ἐμαυτῷ, ὑπὸ νόμον ἤμην. ἐπειδὴ δὲ Χριστὸς ζῇ ἐν ἐμοί, ὁ μηκέτι ὑπὸ νόμον
ἀλλ' ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ πατρός, οὐκ ἀθετῶ τὸν ἐν ἐμοὶ ζῶντα. Ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ
ἐν σαρκί, ἐν πίστει ζῶ. πιστεύω γὰρ εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ. εἰ δὲ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ᾧ
πιστεύω, ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ πατρός, ἐν οὐρανοῖς πολιτεύομαι· ὁ δὲ νόμος ἐν τοῖς ἐπὶ γῆς
εἶχε τὰς τηρήσεις. οὐκ ἄρα ὑπόκειμαι νόμῳ. 301 Gal 3,19–22 Ἐβάρει πλέον ὁ νόμος,
καὶ διακονία θανάτου διὰ τοῦτο ὠνόμασται. πῶς οὖν τῶν παραβάσεων χάριν
προσετέθη, φησίν; ἐν συντόμῳ ῥήματι τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν· πρὸ νόμου καὶ ὁ νοῦς τῶν
ἀνθρώπων μετὰ τῆς σαρκὸς ἐδούλευσε τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ καὶ ἔστεργε τὸ κακόν, δοθέντος
τοῦ νόμου ὁ μὲν νοῦς ἐπαιδεύθη, ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἔτι κατείχετο. ἐπεὶ οὖν ὁ μὲν ἀγνοῶν τὴν
ἁμαρτίαν ὅτι ἁμαρτία ἦν, τὴν ἀσέβειαν ὡς εὐσέβειαν μετιὼν καὶ σπουδαιότερον
αὐτῇ προσέχει, ὁ δὲ γνοὺς ὅτι κακόν, τοῦτο γοῦν κερδανεῖ τὸ συνειδέναι ὅτι
παραβαίνει, καὶ ἐπιθυμεῖ τῷ θεῷ ὑπακοῦσαι. διὰ τοῦτο ἐδόθη νόμος ὁ δυνάμενος
ζωοποιῆσαι, ἀντὶ τοῦ εἰ ἐδόθη νόμος, οὐκ ἐδόθη, φησί, κατὰ τῶν ἐπαγγελιῶν τοῦ
θεοῦ, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ διὰ παντὸς κρατεῖν ἐδύνατο. Gal 3,23 Εἰ καὶ μηδὲν ἕτερον κατώρθου
ὁ νόμος, ἀλλὰ τὸ τὸν θεὸν εἰδέναι παρεῖχεν. τὸ δὲ τὸν θεὸν εἰδέναι ἕτοιμον ἐποίει
πρὸς τὴν τῆς χάριτος ὑποδοχήν. Gal 3,27–28 Οὐχ ἡ τοῦ νόμου τήρησις, φησί,
βελτίονας ποιεῖ τοὺς πιστεύσαντας τῶν ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν τοὺς Ἰουδαίους, ἀλλ' ἡ
δύναμις τοῦ βαπτίσματος τὸ Χριστὸν ἐνδύσασθαι παρέχουσα, κοινὴν ποιεῖ τὴν χάριν
πάντων ὁμοῦ, βαρβάρων, Ἑλλήνων, Ἰουδαίων, θήλεος, ἄρρενος. οὐχ ἁπλῶς δὲ
παρέμιξε τὸ θῆλυ καὶ τὸ ἄρρεν–ὅσον γὰρ εἷς τῷ ῥήματι ἐζήτει πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον–,
ἀλλ' εἰ τὸ ἄρρεν καὶ τὸ θῆλυ διαφέρον εἰς μίαν χάριν συνάγει τὸ βάπτισμα, πόσῳ
μᾶλλον Ἕλληνα καὶ Ἰουδαῖον. Gal 4,8–10 Νῦν βούλεται δεῖξαι ὅτι μετὰ τὸ τὴν χάριν
ἐλθεῖν, κἂν δοκῇ τις κατὰ νόμον σάββατον τηρεῖν καὶ νεομηνίας καὶ ἑορτάς, ὥσπερ
εἰδωλολατρεῖ τοῖς στοιχείοις οἷς ἐθρήσκευεν ἐθνικὸς ὤν, ἄλλως δουλεύων. καὶ οὐ
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing Galatians 2:18 from the previous section] ... to the Antiochenes and to all the inhabited world. It is unfitting, then, to teach these things to others, of whose care (observance) you stood away and which you abolished by your own decree.
Galatians 2:19- (the label is open-ended). The law has the practice and the enjoyment of bodily things: eat this and do not eat that, keep the Sabbath, circumcision. Grace does not want you to be well thought of through these things. I was put to death, then, he says, to these things. What need do I have of law? "And I no longer live, but Christ lives in me." What I lived to myself, I was under law. But since Christ lives in me, who is no longer under law but in the heavens at the right of the Father, I do not set aside the one living in me. "And what I now live in the flesh, I live in faith." For I believe in the Son of God. And if the Son of God, in whom I believe, is at the right hand of the Father, I live as a citizen in the heavens; but the law had its observances among the things on earth. So I am not subject to law.
Galatians 3:19-22. The law weighed down more, and for this reason it has been named a ministry of death. How then was it added for the sake of transgressions, he says? In a short word it is like this: before the law both the mind of human beings, together with the flesh, was a slave to sin and loved evil; when the law had been given, the mind was taught, but the flesh was still held fast. Since, then, the one who does not know sin, that it was sin, pursuing impiety as piety, also attends to it more zealously, while the one who has known that it is evil gains at least this, being conscious that he transgresses, and he desires to obey God. For this reason the law was given. "A law able to make alive" in place of: if a law was given, it was not given, he says, against the promises of God; but neither was it able to hold power through everything (for ever).
Galatians 3:23. Even if the law accomplished nothing else, yet it supplied knowing God. And knowing God made one ready for the reception of grace.
Galatians 3:27-28. Not the keeping of the law, he says, makes the Jews who believed better than those from the nations, but the power of baptism, which provides putting on Christ, makes the grace common of all together: barbarians, Greeks, Jews, female, male. And not simply (without purpose) did he mix in the female and the male, for as much as "one" in the saying was sought toward the matter set before him; but if baptism gathers the male and the female, which differ, into one grace, by how much more Greek and Jew.
Galatians 4:8-10. Now he wants to show that after grace has come, even if someone seems according to the law to keep Sabbath and new moons and feasts, he is as it were worshipping as idols the elements which he worshipped being a Gentile, being a slave in another way. And not [continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: … people of Antioch and to the whole world. So it is unfitting for you to teach others these things, when you yourself have stopped observing them and have abolished them by your own decree.

On Galatians 2:19–20: The law is about bodily things, about doing them and enjoying them: eat this, do not eat that, keep the Sabbath, be circumcised. Grace does not want you to earn approval by such things. So, he says, I have died to them. What need have I of the law? “It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.” While I lived for myself, I was under the law. But since Christ lives in me, and he is no longer under the law but in the heavens at the Father’s right hand, I do not set aside the one who lives in me. “And the life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith”, since I believe in the Son of God. If the Son of God, in whom I believe, is at the Father’s right hand, then my citizenship is in the heavens. The law kept its observances among the things of earth. So I am not subject to the law.

On Galatians 3:19–22: The law was a heavier burden, and that is why it was called a ministry of death (2 Corinthians 3:7). Then how, he asks, was it added because of transgressions? Put briefly, it is like this. Before the law, the human mind, together with the flesh, served sin and was fond of evil. When the law was given, the mind was taught, but the flesh was still held captive. Now, a man who does not know that sin is sin takes up impiety as if it were piety and gives himself to it all the more eagerly. But a man who knows that it is evil gains at least this much: he is aware that he is transgressing, and he longs to obey God. That is why the law was given. “A law that could give life” means this: if a law was given, it was not given, he says, against the promises of God; but neither could it keep its hold for ever.
On Galatians 3:23: Even if the law achieved nothing else, it did give people the knowledge of God. And knowing God made them ready to receive grace.

On Galatians 3:27–28: It is not keeping the law, he says, that makes Jews who have believed better than those who came from the Gentiles. It is the power of baptism, which lets us put on Christ, that makes grace common to all alike: barbarians, Greeks, Jews, female and male. He did not add “female and male” idly, since, as far as the wording goes, “one” was what the point at hand required. Rather, if baptism gathers male and female, different as they are, into one grace, how much more Greek and Jew!

On Galatians 4:8–10: Now he wants to show that once grace has come, anyone who still claims to keep Sabbaths, new moons and feasts by the law is as good as worshipping the elements as idols, the elements he served when he was a pagan. He is a slave again, only in another form. And he does not …

lemmas.gloss: care, attention (to observances); stand away from, abandon
be well thought of, win approval
live as a citizen, have one's citizenship

choices.english: … people of Antioch and to the whole world.
choices.why: Completes the sentence begun at the end of u01-open (decree sent to Antioch); starts with an ellipsis, no text moved.
rejected: To Antioch and to the whole inhabited world. (old: read as a fresh sentence)

choices.term: ὧν τῆς ἐπιμελείας ἀπέστης καὶ ἰδίῳ κατέλυσας δόγματι
choices.english: when you yourself have stopped observing them and have abolished them by your own decree
choices.why: Second person addressed to Peter, as in 2:18 note; the old English made it 'he has settled on his own doctrine'.
rejected: from whose care he has turned away and has settled on his own doctrine

choices.why: The edition label is open-ended; the note quotes and explains 2:19 ('I died') and 2:20 only, so it is labelled 2:19–20.

choices.english: The law was a heavier burden
choices.why: The note starts a new sentence here; the old English began in lower case mid-sentence.
rejected: the law was more burdensome (lower case, no label)

choices.term: διὰ τοῦτο ἐδόθη νόμος ὁ δυνάμενος ζωοποιῆσαι, ἀντὶ τοῦ …
choices.english: That is why the law was given. “A law that could give life” means this: …
choices.why: Read with a stop after νόμος and 'ὁ δυνάμενος ζωοποιῆσαι' as the lemma of Galatians 3:21, explained by ἀντὶ τοῦ; read without the stop, Severian would say the law was given 'able to give life', which Paul denies in that verse. Recorded in translator_notes.
rejected: the law was given, which is able to vivify, instead of 'if the law had been given, it would not have been given' (old, unreadable)

choices.term: ὅσον γὰρ εἷς τῷ ῥήματι ἐζήτει πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον
choices.english: since, as far as the wording goes, “one” was what the point at hand required
choices.why: εἷς taken as the 'one' of Galatians 3:28; the clause is compressed and the rendering stays close to the words. Recorded as uncertain in translator_notes.
rejected: insofar as one sought through the word toward what was set before him (old)

choices.english: is as good as worshipping the elements as idols
choices.why: ὥσπερ softens the charge: 'as it were'.
The sentence ends in u01-rem-mid ('νόμον τηρεῖ'); ellipsis at the break.

bible_refs.note: 2:19– label open-ended in the edition; lemmas 2:20 and 3:21 quoted
